title: The effect of ChatGPT on students’ learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking: insights from a meta-analysis
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether ChatGPT improves student learning outcomes, and under what conditions its effects are strongest. The authors note that while many studies claim benefits, others report null or negative effects, so they conduct a meta-analysis to synthesize the evidence and identify moderators.

The review includes 51 experimental or quasi-experimental studies published between November 2022 and February 2025, yielding 72 independent effect sizes. The included studies span primary, secondary, and college settings, but the analyzed samples are overwhelmingly college-level; the interventions occur across STEM, language/writing, and skills/competencies courses. The paper codes several design features, including grade level, course type, learning model, duration, role of ChatGPT, and application area.

Across studies, ChatGPT shows a large positive effect on learning performance and moderate positive effects on learning perception and higher-order thinking. Effects are stronger in problem-based learning, in 4–8 week interventions for performance, and in longer interventions for learning perception. The authors conclude that ChatGPT can support learning when used as an intelligent tutor, partner, or tool, but its effectiveness depends on instructional design and sustained use. They also argue that future research should better specify how ChatGPT is integrated into teaching and learning, especially for perception and higher-order thinking outcomes.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI’s generative AI chatbot based on GPT models, designed for conversational assistance, text generation, feedback, and tutoring-like interaction.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the focal AI tool in 51 experimental and quasi-experimental studies and synthesized in a meta-analysis to assess its effects on students’ learning performance, learning perception, and higher-order thinking.

findings.finding_summary: Across 44 independent studies, ChatGPT had a large positive effect on learning performance (g=0.867, 95% CI [0.683, 1.052], p<0.001). The meta-analysis reported substantial heterogeneity (Q=399.725, I2=89.243%).
Across 19 independent studies, ChatGPT had a moderate positive effect on learning perception (g=0.456, 95% CI [0.287, 0.625], p<0.001). Heterogeneity was moderate to high (Q=65.646, I2=72.580%).

Across 9 independent studies, ChatGPT had a moderate positive effect on higher-order thinking (g=0.457, 95% CI [0.255, 0.650], p<0.05). The included studies showed moderate heterogeneity (Q=18.105, I2=55.813%).

quality_tier_rationale: This is a meta-analysis of 51 empirical studies with quantitative synthesis and reported effect sizes, confidence intervals, and heterogeneity statistics. That design supports a high evidence tier despite some heterogeneity concerns.
impact_tier_rationale: The primary outcome effect on learning performance is large (g=0.867), and the other reported outcomes are medium-sized (g=0.456 and g=0.457). By the stated threshold, the overall impact is clearly in the medium-to-large range.
